newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Ex-policeman details deaths of 8 children in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Ex-policeman details deaths of 8 children in Brazil.

text.p: A former police officer pleaded guilty on Wednesday to participating in the shooting deaths of eight street children more than three years ago near a Rio de Janeiro church, a crime that caused worldwide outcry.
Nelson Oliveira dos Santos Cunha, 29, who resigned from the Rio police force after the massacre, went on trial in Rio de Janeiro state court on Wednesday.

He had confessed his role in the killings to police last April and has been in police custody since then. His confession came just days before the first of five men accused of participating in the July 23, 1993 massacre went on trial.

In his testimony on Wednesday, Cunha blamed one police officer, who has since been murdered, for most of the killings, but admitted to having accidentally shot and wounded one of the victims of the shooting spree, Wagner dos Santos, who is also a key witness.

Cunha, a born-again Christian who says God made him confess, said he and three other policemen picked up Santos and two minors near the Candelaria Church in the centre of Rio and bundled them into their car.

Cunha said he was frightened sitting in the back seat with Santos who looked quite strong, so he took out his gun to keep him under control. "I was nervous in the back of the car, I pulled out my gun. We drove over a pothole and the gun went off and hit Wagner," he said.

The police officers then drove the three youngsters a short distance away, dragged them from the car and shot all three and left them for dead, but Santos survived. Cunha said he heard the shots from the car, but did not see who fired.

Cunha said the policemen then drove to the Candelaria Church where the police officer who has since died opened fire on about 70 children playing or sleeping on the steps of the church. Six children died and six were wounded.

Santos, 24, who returned to Rio on Monday from Switzerland, where he fled after two attempts on his life after the killings, claimed he does not recognise Cunha as one of the killers and has named another police officer as his main attacker, according to his lawyer Cristina Leonardo.
Santos has identified Lt. Marcelo Ferreira Cortes in connection with the massacre, but Cunha says he did not take part.

Daniels said the real test case would be Cortes, who goes on trial on Dec. 9 along with two others, because he is a higher ranking police officer than Cunha or Marcus Vinicius Borges Emmanuel, who was sentenced to 309 years in jail in the April trial. Emmanuel's sentence was later cut by 220 years at a retrial. Cunha faces a similar sentence of several life terms if he is convicted.
Yvonne Bezerra de Melo, an artist who has worked with the Candelaria street children since before the massacre, said Cunha's account does not correspond with that of the children.

"The children say they saw six or seven men shooting at them," de Melo said. "Three guns were used. It is hard to believe that only one person is supposed to have carried out this kind of a slaughter."

The National Movement of Streetchildren says four minors are killed every day in Brazil, mostly by police, death squads that often include off-duty police officers, or drug gangs. About 90 percent of cases never make it to court.
